setup.android_hint: No certificate installation needed on Android. Scan the QR code, and if your browser warns about the local self-signed certificate, simply tap `Advanced` → `Proceed to site (unsafe)` or confirm trust.
setup.disclosure_body_1: **What am I installing?** A small security certificate, generated right on your own PC — nothing about it ever leaves your local network. It just tells your phone "trust this one connection" so it can talk to your computer over Wi-Fi. It can't see or touch anything else — not your other apps, not other websites, nothing. The app doesn't send any data anywhere, ever — no analytics, no logs, no phoning home. And since it's all open-source, you don't have to take our word for it: you (or your AI coding assistant) can go read the exact code that generates this certificate right here: [`internal/ca`](https://github.com/MrHoustonOff/iphone-gyro-controller/tree/main/internal/ca).
setup.disclosure_body_2: **Why is this even necessary?** Safari (WebKit) simply refuses to share gyroscope/motion data or keep a live WebSocket connection open unless the page is loaded over a secure, encrypted connection (HTTPS/WSS) — that's an Apple privacy rule, and no app can get around it. Since there's no way to get a "real," publicly-trusted certificate for a private local address, self-signing one and asking your phone to trust it is the only way to satisfy that rule without ever going through the internet.
setup.disclosure_body_3: **The trade-off:** you get a fully private, direct, offline connection where none of your data ever leaves your Wi-Fi — but in exchange, you have to do this one manual "trust" step yourself, since there's no public authority that can vouch for a certificate that only exists on your home network.

setup.ios_desc: One-time local profile setup for Safari
setup.ios_step1_text: Open the link (or scan the QR code) **on your phone**, then tap `Allow`.
setup.ios_step2_text: Go to `Settings`. A banner reading `Profile Downloaded` will appear at the top of the screen — tap it.
setup.ios_step5_text: Return to the main `Settings` screen. Go to `General` → `About`, then scroll all the way down to `Certificate Trust Settings` and tap it.
setup.ios_step6_text: You'll see your certificate listed. Toggle it on, then tap `Continue`.
